question.message:
The project has no files and no case, and no Knowledge document covers this town, so I need the time axis and the demand from you. Please give each with its unit:

TIME AXIS
- time.start, time.end (excluded) and time.step: the period and step of the run (e.g. 2027-01-01 to 2028-01-01, 1 d).
- time_zone: the IANA zone of the demand series' timestamps (e.g. Europe/Amsterdam), if they carry no UTC offset. gemini refuses a series without one.

HEATING DEMAND
- demand.heating.power: the heating demand as a series (a CSV file with a time column, or the values themselves) or a constant power in MW. A peak plus an annual energy cannot be turned into a series, so I need one of those three.
- demand.heating.supply_temperature in °C (the temperature the network must deliver).
- demand.heating.return_temperature in °C (colder than the supply).
- demand.heating.return_pressure in bar, if the network states one.

COOLING (only if the town has a cooling service — say so if it has none, and I leave cooling out)
- demand.cooling.power: series or constant, in MW.
- demand.cooling.supply_temperature and demand.cooling.return_temperature in °C (return warmer than supply).
- demand.cooling.return_pressure in bar; demand.cooling.indoor_temperature in °C; demand.cooling.indoor_relative_humidity as a fraction 0-1.

answer.text: A town of about 5000 homes near Trondheim, Norway. Heating only, about 20 MW peak. We have no demand file. Use your own reasonable assumptions for anything else.

Nothing is saved yet. The project has no files and no case, and no Knowledge document covers this town, so every value below is my own engineering assumption (or a design choice) for a heating-only geothermal district-heating plant near Trondheim, Norway. On approve all the case is set with these; you may also type values instead.

TIME
- time.start = 2027-01-01 | engineering assumption | a full calendar year, the usual run length
- time.end = 2028-01-01 (excluded) | engineering assumption | one year after the start
- time.step = 1 d | engineering assumption | daily steps
- time_zone = Europe/Oslo | engineering assumption | the site is near Trondheim, Norway, and the dates carry no offset

DEMAND (heating only; you gave about 20 MW peak and no file)
- demand.heating.power = 20 MW, constant | engineering assumption | no series exists, and a constant power is the only form available without one; 20 MW is the peak you gave (a daily series would be better — you can give values instead)
- demand.heating.supply_temperature = 90 degC | engineering assumption | a typical Norwegian district-heating supply
- demand.heating.return_temperature = 50 degC | design choice, the brief leaves it to the team | colder than the supply, so the brine can be cooled deeply
- demand.heating.return_pressure = 6 bar | engineering assumption | a typical network return pressure

SITE — ground
- site.ground.surface_temperature = 5 degC | engineering assumption | mean annual air temperature near Trondheim
- site.ground.gradient = 25 °C/km | engineering assumption | a typical gradient for Norwegian bedrock

SITE — reservoir
- site.reservoir.reference_depth = 2000 m | engineering assumption | the depth at which the pressure below holds
- site.reservoir.thickness = 100 m | engineering assumption | a typical reservoir thickness
- site.reservoir.permeability = 200 mD | engineering assumption | a typical value for a productive reservoir
- site.reservoir.pressure = 200 barg | engineering assumption | hydrostatic at 2000 m

SITE — brine
- site.fluid.density = 1030 kg/m3 | engineering assumption | a typical geothermal brine
- site.fluid.viscosity = 0.4 mPa.s | engineering assumption | a typical geothermal brine
- site.fluid.gas_liquid_ratio = 0.5 Nm3/m3 | engineering assumption | a modest dissolved-gas content
- site.fluid.dissolved_gas.CH4 = 0.8, CO2 = 0.2 (mole fraction) | engineering assumption | a typical produced-gas composition
- site.fluid.sand_concentration = 20 mg/l | engineering assumption | a typical sand load

SITE — air
- site.air.temperature = 5 degC, constant | engineering assumption | the site's mean air temperature
- site.air.pressure = 101325 Pa | engineering assumption | sea-level pressure

UTILITIES
- utilities.electricity.co2_intensity = 30 g/kWh | engineering assumption | the Norwegian grid is dominated by hydropower

REQUIREMENTS
- heat_delivered: on heating_supply, unmet_share, max 0.01 | engineering assumption | the heat demand shall be met; 1 % is the tolerance I propose

Not set, and left open: the reservoir temperature (gemini derives it from the ground), the well depth and the number of doublets (design freedoms), the bought-gas composition (only if the design uses a gas boiler), and the electricity import/export limits (no grid operator is given).

Economics of the case, from the cost catalogue.
Site is near Trondheim, Norway: no Norwegian row exists, so the Nordic heat tariff (Sweden) and the EU electricity and gas prices are recommended over the Dutch rows; the discount rate is the real geothermal rate of PBL SDE++ 2025. The four per-energy O&M rows are given because the case is heating-only. No subsidy is named, so every revenue.subsidy key stays open.
